First day on the Somme.question: Since _____ July 1916, the British casualties on the First Day and the "meagre gains" have been a source of grief and controversy in Britain
First day on the Somme.fact: Several truces were observed to recover wounded from no man's land on the British front; the Third Army diversion at Gommecourt cost 6,758 casualties against 1,212 German and the combined casualty count with the Fourth Army reached 57,470, (19,240 of which had been fatal). First day on the Somme.fact: Companies were arranged in columns of platoons, creating four platoon waves 70 yd (64 m) apart.

First day on the Somme.fact: The British artillery fired more than 1.5 million shells during the preliminary bombardment, more than in the first year of the war.

First day on the Somme.subject: Indian Society

First day on the Somme.fact: While this weight of bombardment was new for the British, it was common on the Western Front; at the Second Battle of Artois in May 1915, there had been a six-day preparatory bombardment with over 2.1 million shells.

First day on the Somme.subject: Indian Society
First day on the Somme.question: By mid-1916 much of the _____ infantry in the Sixth Army were specialist rifle-and-bayonet men, bombers, rifle grenadiers or light machine-gun crews
First day on the Somme.fact: In the French army, the experience of 1915 showed that despite the power of French bombardments, infantry would enter a chaotic environment, full of German pockets of resistance and individuals who had been by-passed. By mid-1916 much of the French infantry in the Sixth Army were specialist rifle-and-bayonet men, bombers, rifle grenadiers or light machine-gun crews.

First day on the Somme.subject: Indian Society
First day on the Somme.question: Eight large and eleven small mines were prepared for the first day of the battle; three large mines of up to _____ long tons (24 t) and seven mines around 5,000 lb (2.2 long tons)
First day on the Somme.fact: Eight large and eleven small mines were prepared for the first day of the battle; three large mines of up to 24 long tons (24 t) and seven mines around 5,000 lb (2.2 long tons). When the mines were blown, infantry were to rush forward to seize the craters; the largest mines, each containing 24 long tons (24 t) of ammonal, were on either side of the Albert–Bapaume road near La Boisselle, Y Sap mine north of the road and Lochnagar mine to the south.

First day on the Somme.subject: Indian Society

First day on the Somme.fact: In the 37th Division area, 91,420 man-hours were needed to dig 3.7 mi (6 km) of trenches, jumping-off points, command-posts, dug-outs, machine-gun emplacements and ammunition stores, for wiring and for maintenance.

First day on the Somme.subject: Indian Society

First day on the Somme.fact: Rawlinson favoured a methodical attack from the beginning of the offensive, in which belts of the German defences about 2,000 yd (1,800 m) deep, would be pulverised by artillery and then occupied by infantry.

First day on the Somme.subject: Indian Society

First day on the Somme.fact: Haig became more optimistic at what could be achieved early in an offensive, given the examples of Gorlice-Tarnów in 1915 and at Verdun early in 1916. On 16 April, Rawlinson announced the objectives to the corps commanders, in which III, X and VIII corps would capture Pozières, Grandcourt and Serre on the first day and XIII and XV corps would have objectives to be agreed later.

First day on the Somme.fact: The 2nd and 3rd Colonial divisions, advanced between XXXV Corps and the river and overran the first line of the German 121st Division, holding the line south from the Somme, in fifteen minutes, taking Dompierre-Bequincourt. First day on the Somme.fact: More railway activity, fresh digging and camp extensions around Albert opposite the 2nd Army was seen by German air observers on 9 and 11 June; spies reported an imminent offensive. On 24 June, a British prisoner spoke of a five-day bombardment to begin on 26 June and local units expected an attack within days.

First day on the Somme.subject: Indian Society
First day on the Somme.question: The 7th _____ suffered 3,380 casualties
First day on the Somme.fact: The 7th Division suffered 3,380 casualties. The 20th Brigade, 7th Division, was to capture the west end of Mametz and swing left, creating a defensive flank along Willow Stream, facing Fricourt from the south, as the 22nd Brigade waited in the British front line, ready to exploit a German retirement from the village.

The 20th Brigade, 7th Division, was to capture the west end of Mametz and swing left, creating a defensive flank along Willow Stream, facing Fricourt from the south, as the 22nd Brigade waited in the British front line, ready to exploit a German retirement from the village.

First day on the Somme.fact: XV Corps was to attack either side of the village, to isolate the defenders.

First day on the Somme.fact: The rest of the regimental reserves were used to block the route to Contalmaison.

First day on the Somme.subject: Indian Society

First day on the Somme.fact: The survivors were captured after making the furthest British advance of the day, about 4,000 yd (2.3 mi; 3.7 km).

First day on the Somme.subject: Indian Society
First day on the Somme.question: The 34th _____ suffered the worst casualties of the day, 6,380
First day on the Somme.fact: The III Corps attack on both sides of the Albert–Bapaume road was a disaster, making only a short advance south of La Boisselle, where the 34th Division suffered the most casualties of any Allied division on 1 July. Further north, X Corps captured part of the Leipzig Redoubt (an earthwork fortification), failed opposite Thiepval and had a great but temporary success on the left flank, where the German front line was overrun and Schwaben and Stuff redoubts captured by the 36th (Ulster) Division.
